anomaly_def.Name: Database Memory Allocation Anomaly + CPU Resource Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Database Memory Allocation Anomaly : Excessive growth of database memory regions (buffer/plan caches, work areas, parallel-worker buffers, etc.) drives the host beyond its safe physical or virtual memory envelope.
CPU Resource Anomaly : Database processes collectively saturate available CPU cores, exhausting compute bandwidth irrespective of the individual query or plan inefficiencies behind the demand.

When both anomalies surface together, the system shows a mix of memory-pressure and compute-pressure symptoms: resident-set sizes and swap traffic rise while run-queue depth and context-switch rates spike; page-fault handling, memory-reclaim daemons, and database background threads all compete for CPU, inflating overall latency. Query response times, log-flush and checkpoint operations, and cluster heartbeat intervals all elongate, and node evictions or OOM kills may coincide with scheduler wait events and spin-loop back-offs. Performance counters oscillate unpredictably as memory thrashing generates additional CPU load, making it difficult to attribute slowdowns to a single layer.

Causal chain: memory bloat forces the OS to spend more CPU cycles on page management; the resulting page-fault storms amplify CPU saturation. In turn, CPU starvation slows down individual queries and background tasks, prolonging their memory retention windows and causing further cache/work-area inflation. Parallel workers spawned to speed up lagging queries multiply both the memory footprint and the CPU demand, closing a feedback loop that rapidly depletes remaining resources. The intertwined pressure on memory and compute therefore reinforces itself, accelerating degradation until workload throttling, component failure, or manual intervention occurs.

entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
